title: Photo 214 · 콜로설 · 포다이트 · 비스듬히 기대앉기 · 북유럽 30대 후반
prompt:
Image format: a horizontal landscape-orientation photograph, 3:2 aspect ratio, wider than it is tall.

A full-body photograph on a plain seamless deep-charcoal backdrop, nothing in the frame but a low flat platform with a plain padded backrest at one end, shot on a medium format camera with an 85mm lens at f/8, a single hard key light raking in from one side so the texture of the skin stands out, sharp focus from head to toe, realistic photographic grain — a real photograph, not an illustration, not CGI, not a render.

Subject: ONE real adult Scandinavian woman in her late 30s, very fair skin tone with cool pink undertones and faint freckling across the shoulders, her face exactly the same tone as her body, real skin texture with visible pores and fine grain, thick twin braids over her shoulders, a calm confident expression, real living eyes. She wears heavy ball-drop earrings and has long coffin nails with an iridescent glaze.

Physique: An extraordinarily large woman, far beyond any real person, her body so long and vast that her head and her feet are cut off by the left and right edges of the frame. A giantess built on a completely even scale, every part of her enlarged by the same amount: massive rounded shoulders, huge thick arms, a colossal full bust, a broad heavy torso with a large smooth rounded belly, wide solid hips, enormous columnar thighs and thick heavy calves, a full round face. Her head looks small on top of her massive body, her shoulders span more than four head-widths, each hand is as wide as a normal woman's torso and each thigh thicker than a normal woman's waist. No single part stands out more than another, no hanging folds, not pregnant, her whole body scaled up together into one immense smooth silhouette that towers over the viewer. Every fold and curve keeps its own clear rounded outline with a deep shadowed crease between them, never merging into one shapeless mass. Her arms, hands, legs and feet stay in correct proportion to each other. The sheer weight of the flesh is visible in how it spills forward down her body, settles and presses flat against the platform beneath her.

Skin: Real photographic skin — visible pores and fine grain, natural creases and shadow where the flesh folds, faint stretch marks where the great curves have expanded, the raking light picking out every ridge and hollow of the surface. No smooth illustration finish, no plastic CG sheen.

Body Art: Her bare skin is painted in polished fordite style — thin layered strata of candy red, teal, mustard yellow, cobalt, white and orange stacked in tight concentric bands that follow every deep crease and curve around the hips and thighs like contour lines. The paint is pigment sitting on living skin, so it distorts slightly over every bulge and cracks a little where the skin folds. The paint covers her whole body with no bare skin left anywhere below the jaw: her shoulders, her upper arms, her forearms and the backs of her hands are painted as densely as her torso, and so are the sides of her body, her back, her rear, the lower belly, the knees, the calves and the tops of her feet. Her face is left unpainted and the pattern fades out at the neck with no hard line.

Pose: Reclining on the platform propped up against the backrest at about 45 degrees, her legs stretched out straight in front of her and slightly apart, her arms resting back on the platform behind her hips with the elbows out so nothing crosses in front of her torso, her head turned toward the camera, her colossal hips and rear spreading wide and flattening against the platform, her body stretching across the full width of the frame from edge to edge.

Footwear: Extreme candy-red platform stiletto mules with a scalloped edge, the platform soles as tall as her ankle bones, the ultra-thin stiletto heels so high her insteps stand nearly vertical.

Background & Lighting: the layered colour bands gleaming, the hard raking light carving every fold and curve.

Horizontal 3:2 landscape-orientation full-body photograph, wider than it is tall.
